note: Hand-written from Google's Chirp 3 HD phoneme table for the locale where one exists (fr-FR, es-ES, it-IT) and from PHOIBLE otherwise; first draft 2026-10-16. Symbols are the phonemic set an entry may use; the display and the engine input share it.
conventions: Standard Italian. Geminates carry ː on the consonant (fatto is /ˈfatːo/); a geminate affricate doubles its stop instead (oggi is /ˈɔddʒi/, pizza is /ˈpittsa/), and ʃ ʎ ɲ between vowels are written long (pesce is /ˈpeʃːe/). Open and close e and o are distinguished (ɛ/e, ɔ/o) in stressed syllables and are e, o when unstressed. Intervocalic s is z where the standard has it.
